review_evidence: Codex self-review: pedagogy, answer keys, concept slots, unseen passages, age fit, and source independence
title: Colours
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: Share the colour, explain the help
levels.focus: infer why sharing helps and give a reason
levels.teaching_goal: Use what each child has and needs to explain how sharing helps both children.

guided_check.teaching_block: To answer a why question, join two clues. Leena has blue, Omar needs blue, so sharing lets Omar finish his sea.
guided_check.passage: Leena has a blue crayon. Omar has a yellow crayon. Omar needs blue for the sea, and Leena needs yellow for the sun.
guided_check.prompt: Why will sharing help both children?
options: Each child can use the colour they need.
Both children will lose a crayon.
accepted_answers: Each child can use the colour they need.
each child can use the colour they need

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge steps: name the need, name the helpful action, then name the result. Here both painters need the colour held by the other painter.
bridge.passage: Pia has green paint for leaves. Zoya has red paint for apples. Pia also needs red, and Zoya also needs green.
bridge.prompt: Which action should come before both paintings are complete?

masterclass.teaching_block: A common mistake is to think sharing means giving everything away. Sharing can mean taking turns or lending a little, so both people can continue.
masterclass.passage: There is one silver crayon. Jai uses it for a moon, then passes it to Noor for a star.
masterclass.prompt: What shows that Jai and Noor shared fairly?
options: They took turns with the crayon.
Jai kept the crayon all day.
accepted_answers: They took turns with the crayon.

independent_check.teaching_block: Now connect the need, action, and result on your own.
independent_check.passage: Ritu has orange and white clay. Manav has purple and black clay. Their model needs all four colours.
independent_check.prompt: Explain how the two children can finish the model together.

concept_slots.description: says that they share or exchange clay
says that both can use all four colours or finish the model

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use the same reason pattern in a new kind of classroom task.
transfer_check.passage: For a nature chart, Isha has leaf stamps and Tanu has flower stamps. Both charts need leaves and flowers.
transfer_check.prompt: What should Isha and Tanu do, and why?

concept_slots.description: suggests sharing, swapping, or taking turns with the stamps
explains that both charts can include leaves and flowers

levels.title: Match colour words to their clues
levels.focus: use sentence context to connect a colour with the right object
levels.teaching_goal: Read nearby words to decide which object a colour describes and what an unfamiliar shade means.

guided_check.teaching_block: A describing word often sits near the naming word it belongs to. Read the whole sentence before choosing.
guided_check.passage: A bright red ladybird rested on a pale green leaf.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge steps: first circle the object in your mind, then look beside it for its colour word.
bridge.passage: The child tied a pink ribbon around the parcel.
bridge.prompt: What does the word pink describe?

masterclass.teaching_block: Do not choose the nearest colour automatically when two objects appear. Match each colour to the noun it directly describes.
masterclass.passage: A white shell lay beside a golden coin.

independent_check.teaching_block: Read the new sentence without a clue step.
independent_check.passage: Mili placed a violet cup on a grey tray.
independent_check.prompt: Write the colour of the tray.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer the context strategy to a less familiar colour word.
transfer_check.passage: At sunset, the clouds looked crimson, a deep red colour above the hills.
transfer_check.prompt: What colour does crimson mean here?

levels.title: Find who, what, and how
levels.focus: separate naming, action, and describing words
levels.teaching_goal: Use a word's job in a sentence to distinguish nouns, verbs, and colour adjectives.

guided_check.teaching_block: A naming word names a person, place, animal, or thing. An action word tells what happens. A describing word adds a detail such as colour.
guided_check.passage: The cheerful children paint a blue wall.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge test: ask, 'Can someone do it?' A person can splash, so splash is an action word.
bridge.passage: Two artists splash yellow paint on the paper.

masterclass.teaching_block: Colour words are usually describing words, not actions. In 'She colours the card,' colours is an action because it tells what she does.
masterclass.passage: Aarav colours the round mask with purple ink.
masterclass.prompt: Which word is the action in this sentence?

independent_check.teaching_block: Decide the word job without the test being shown.
independent_check.passage: The tiny brush spreads silver paint.
independent_check.prompt: Write the describing word that tells size.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use word jobs in a new setting away from an art table.
transfer_check.passage: The cook slices a green cucumber.

levels.title: Build a colour-word index
levels.focus: order words by first and second letters
levels.teaching_goal: Arrange colour words alphabetically, using the next letter when first letters match.

guided_check.teaching_block: Alphabetical order follows A to Z. Compare the first letters: b in blue comes before g in green and r in red.
guided_check.prompt: Which order would place these cards in a word index?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge steps: write only the first letters, order those letters, then put each full word back.
bridge.passage: First letters for violet, amber, and teal are v, a, and t.

masterclass.teaching_block: When two words begin with the same letter, the first letter cannot decide. Compare the second letters: l in black comes before r in brown.
masterclass.passage: Two colour labels begin with b: black and brown.

independent_check.teaching_block: Order all the words without letter hints.
independent_check.passage: Colour list: white, orange, pink, grey.
independent_check.prompt: Put the four colour words in alphabetical order.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer alphabetising to a classroom list that is not about colours.
transfer_check.passage: Art-box list: ruler, eraser, brush, pencil.
transfer_check.prompt: Arrange the four words in alphabetical order.

levels.title: Join word friends and use them
levels.focus: form compound words and write a complete idea
levels.teaching_goal: Join two words in the correct order to make a compound word, then use that word in a meaningful sentence.

guided_check.teaching_block: A compound word joins two smaller words to make one new meaning. Rain plus bow makes rainbow.
guided_check.passage: After the shower, seven colours curved across the sky: rain + bow.
guided_check.prompt: Which compound word names the coloured arc?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge steps: read the first part, read the second part, then say them without a pause.
bridge.passage: The warm light comes from sun + light.

masterclass.teaching_block: The order of the parts matters. A sunflower is a kind of flower; flowersun is not an English word.
masterclass.passage: A tall yellow bloom turns towards the sun.
masterclass.prompt: Which word correctly names the bloom?

independent_check.teaching_block: Make the compound word without choices.
independent_check.passage: A small bird sits near the water + fall.
independent_check.prompt: Join the two words to name the place.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use a compound word to create a new complete message.
transfer_check.passage: A class display shows a bright rainbow above paper houses.
transfer_check.prompt: Write one complete sentence about the display using the word rainbow.

concept_slots.description: states a complete idea about what the rainbow does or looks like

concept_slots.description: explains that both groups can make or finish the badges

items.passage: Naman lends his gold pen after finishing his border. Alia can now finish her stars.
accepted_answers: it helped alia finish her stars

items.passage: Sara has sponge stamps. Vihaan has paint rollers. Their poster needs both textures.
items.prompt: Tell what they can do and how it will improve the poster.

concept_slots.description: suggests sharing, swapping, or taking turns with tools
connects the action to using both textures or finishing the poster

items.passage: A turquoise boat crossed the dark lake. Turquoise is a blue-green shade.
items.prompt: What does turquoise mean in this sentence?

items.passage: A black ant crawled across a cream plate.
items.prompt: Write the colour of the plate.

A copper bell shone with a reddish-brown colour in the light.
The careful artist mixes pale paint.

items.prompt: Write the naming word for the object that glows.

items.passage: The noisy children carry orange flags.
Mina folds the wide purple sheet.
items.prompt: Which verb tells what Mina does?

Index words: bronze, beige, black.
